title: Emit a machine-readable engine version
summary: The `forgel` engine reports its version in a stable machine-readable form that an installer or a client can read and compare without parsing prose. This is the foundation for the version comparison and the startup check in later tasks.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

checks.criterion: A single request to the engine for its version in machine-readable form yields one JSON object on standard output, parseable without preprocessing, with nothing else emitted on standard output, nothing on standard error, and a successful exit status.
A reader taking the version value from that object obtains the same string as the engine's own declared version and as the human-readable version report.
The version value splits into at least three numeric components and can be ordered against another value of the same shape without reading prose.
The same request run in a clean environment with no project, no session, no model configuration and no network access still yields the version report and succeeds.
After the request, no file was created or modified in the working directory, the project artifacts or the user's Forgel home.
The existing human-readable version output is unchanged in content and exit status.
Automated tests exercise the machine-readable report's shape, its value agreement and its availability without configuration; the project test suite passes.

external_dependencies.name: Semantic-style dotted version ordering
external_dependencies.interface: Order two engine versions by their numeric components: split the reported dotted string on '.', convert each component with int(), and compare the resulting tuples/numbers. This is pure Python standard-library logic (int(), str.split(), tuple comparison) with no third-party package, command or service involved, so an installer or client can compare the reported engine version against another version deterministically.
external_dependencies.docs: https://semver.org/ ; Python standard library comparison semantics (int()/str.split()/tuple ordering)
external_dependencies.evidence: The task's dependency entry states the contract: 'an installer or client reads the reported version value and orders it against another engine version by its numeric components; docs: https://semver.org/'. The project's own instructions (FORGEL.md, 'Runtime Process Model') reference the engine source as `src/forgel/runtime_model.py`, i.e. the engine is a Python package under `src/forgel/`, so numeric-component ordering is available locally from the Python standard library (split on '.', int() each part, compare tuples) without installing anything. semver.org defines the dotted numeric ordering being consumed.

external_dependencies.name: JSON
external_dependencies.interface: Emit the machine-readable version report as exactly one JSON object on standard output, produced with Python's standard-library `json` module (json.dumps), and read/parsed with json.loads. No third-party JSON library, external command or service is used.
external_dependencies.evidence: The task's dependency entry states the contract explicitly: 'the machine-readable report is one JSON object on standard output; reading it uses only the standard library; docs: —'. The engine is a Python package under `src/forgel/` (FORGEL.md refers to `src/forgel/runtime_model.py`), so the standard-library `json` module is present in the runtime and satisfies the 'only the standard library' clause; no installation or external interface is required.
